# Esther Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 457r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EST_003_page_001.jpg

---

**3:1** After these things [hadevarim], King Ahasuerus promoted [giddal] Haman [Haman] son of Hammedatha [Hammedatha] the Agagite [ha'Agagi], and he exalted him [vayenas'ehu] and set [vayyasem] his seat [kis'o] above all the officials [hasarim] who were with him.

**3:2** And all the servants [avdei] of the king who were in the gate [sha'ar] of the king were bowing down [kor'im] and prostrating themselves [umishtachavim] to Haman, for thus the king had commanded [tzivvah] concerning him. But Mordecai [Mordekhai] would not bow down [lo yikhra] and would not prostrate himself [velo yishtachaveh].

**3:3** And the servants of the king who were in the gate of the king said to Mordecai, "Why do you transgress [over] the command [mitzvat] of the king?"

**3:4** And it was, when they spoke to him day [yom] after day [vayom] and he would not listen [velo shama] to them, that they told Haman, to see whether the words [divrei] of Mordecai would stand [ya'amdu], for he had told [higgid] them that he was a Jew [yehudi].

**3:5** And Haman saw [vayyar] that Mordecai would not bow down and would not prostrate himself to him, and Haman was filled [vayyimmale] with wrath [chemah].

**3:6** But it was contemptible [vayyivez] in his eyes to send a hand [lishloach yad] against Mordecai alone, for they had told him the people [am] of Mordecai. And Haman sought [vayevaqesh] to destroy [lehash'mid] all the Jews [hayyehudim] who were in all the kingdom [malkhut] of Ahasuerus — the people [am] of Mordecai.

**3:7** In the first month [bachodesh harishon] — that is, the month of Nisan [chodesh Nisan] — in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, the Pur [Pur] — that is, the lot [haggoral] — was cast [hippil] before Haman from day [miyyom] to day [leyom] and from month [mecchodesh] to month [lechodesh], to the twelfth month — that is, the month of Adar [chodesh Adar].

**3:8** And Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is a certain people [am echad], scattered [mefuzzar] and separated [umforad] among the peoples [ha'ammim] in all the provinces [medinot] of your kingdom, and their laws [dateihem] are different [shonot] from every people [am], and the laws [datei] of the king they do not do [ein osim], and it is not fitting [ein shoveh] for the king to let them remain [lehanniacham].

**3:9** If it is good [tov] upon the king, let it be written [yikkatev] to destroy them [le'abbedam], and ten thousand talents [aseret alafim kikkar] of silver [kesef] I will weigh out [eshqol] upon the hands of those who do the work [osei hammelakhah], to bring it into the treasuries [ginzei] of the king."

**3:10** And the king removed [vayyasar] his signet ring [tabba'ato] from upon his hand and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the adversary [tzorer] of the Jews.

**3:11** And the king said to Haman, "The silver [hakkesef] is given [natun] to you, and the people [ha'am] also, to do with them as is good [kattov] in your eyes."

**3:12** And the scribes [soferei] of the king were called [vayyiqare'u] in the first month, on the thirteenth day of it, and it was written [vayyikkatev] according to all that Haman commanded — to the satraps [achashdarpnei] of the king and to the governors [hapachot] who were over each province and to the officials [sarei] of each people, each province according to its script [kikhtvah] and each people according to its tongue [kilshono]. In the name [beshem] of King Ahasuerus it was written, and it was sealed [venechttam] with the king's signet ring [betabba'at hammelekh].

**3:13** And letters [sefarim] were sent [venishlach] by the hand of runners [haratzim] to all the provinces of the king — to destroy [lehash'mid], to kill [laharog], and to annihilate [ule'abbed] all the Jews, from young [minna'ar] to old [ve'ad zaqen], children [taf] and women [venashim], in one day [beyom echad], on the thirteenth of the twelfth month — that is, the month of Adar — and to plunder [velishlolam] their possessions [shelalm].

**3:14** A copy [patshegen] of the writing [hakketav] was to be given [lehinnatten] as a decree [dat] in every province, published [galuy] to all the peoples, to be ready [lehiyot atidim] for that day.

**3:15** The runners went out [yatze'u], hastened [dechufim] by the word [bidvar] of the king, and the decree [haddat] was given [nittenah] in Susa the citadel. And the king and Haman sat down [yashvu] to drink [lishtot], but the city [ha'ir] of Susa was in confusion [navokah].

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **Ha'Agagi (3:1):** "The Agagite" — this epithet links Haman to Agag, king of the Amalekites (1 Samuel 15), establishing the conflict between Haman and Mordecai as a continuation of the ancient enmity between Amalek and Israel, and specifically between the house of Saul (a Benjaminite like Mordecai's ancestor Kish) and Agag.

2. **Pur/Haggoral (3:7):** The narrator glosses the Persian word *Pur* with the Hebrew *haggoral* ("the lot"). This word gives the festival of Purim its name. The casting of lots to determine the date of destruction introduces an element of fate or chance — which the narrative will ultimately subvert.

3. **Lehash'mid, laharog, ule'abbed (3:13):** Three verbs of destruction — "to destroy, to kill, and to annihilate" — a tripled intensification that conveys the totality of the intended genocide. The same three-verb formula will be reversed in 8:11 when the Jews receive permission to defend themselves.

4. **Navokah (3:15):** "Was in confusion" — the city of Susa itself recoils from the decree, while the king and Haman sit drinking. This stark juxtaposition closes the chapter with devastating irony.

*— EMET*
